record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.context_brief: Cayley description of planar codimension-1 strata
record.original_question: For a given graph G in the plane, does there exist a Cayley algebra system, or finitely many such systems, whose solution set is exactly the union of the codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the planar configuration space B_2(G)?

evidence.quote: One of the main long-standing open problems on the Cayley strata description is as follows.

Problem 7 Given a graph G. Does there exist a Cayley algebra system (or several systems) describing the union of the codimension 1 tensegrity strata in the plane [i.e., the union of the codimension 1 strata of B2(Kn)]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite graph with $n=|V|$ vertices. A planar configuration of $G$ is a map $p\colon V\to\mathbb{R}^2$ assigning to each vertex $v_i$ a point $p_i\in\mathbb{R}^2$. Identify the configuration space of $G$ in the plane with $B_2(G)=(\mathbb{R}^2)^V$ (or, equivalently, with the configuration space of the complete graph $B_2(K_n)$ when one ignores the edge structure of $G$).

A self-stress (or equilibrium stress) on $G$ at $p$ is an assignment of real weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$ to the edges $\{v_i,v_j\}\in E$ such that, for every vertex $v_i$,
$$\sum_{j:\,\{v_i,v_j\}\in E} w_{ij}\,(p_j-p_i)=0.$$
A tensegrity is a configuration $p$ together with a self-stress $w$ in which the signs of the weights are prescribed (cables, struts, bars). The tensegrity stratification of $B_2(G)$ is the partition of the configuration space according to the sign pattern (and the dimension of the space) of self-stresses supported on $G$ at $p$. Each stratum is a semi-algebraic subset of $B_2(G)$, and one defines the codimension-$1$ strata in the usual way (those of codimension exactly $1$ in $B_2(G)$).

The (planar) Cayley algebra is the algebraic system whose elements are points and lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$, equipped with two partial operations: the join $\vee$ which sends a pair of points to the line through them, and the meet $\wedge$ which sends a pair of lines to their intersection point. A Cayley algebra system is a finite system of equalities/incidence conditions built from variable points (the $p_i$) and from terms obtained by iterated application of $\vee$ and $\wedge$; its solution set is the locus in $B_2(G)$ of configurations $p$ satisfying all conditions of the system. A finite collection of Cayley algebra systems is said to describe a subset $S\subseteq B_2(G)$ if $S$ equals the union of the solution sets of these systems.

Problem. For an arbitrary finite graph $G$, does there exist a Cayley algebra system, or a finite collection of Cayley algebra systems, whose union of solution sets coincides exactly with the union of all codimension-$1$ tensegrity strata in the planar configuration space $B_2(G)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as a long-standing open problem about Cayley-style descriptions of codimension-1 tensegrity strata in the plane. A weaker version (using an extended Cayley algebra with extra auxiliary elements) has been resolved, but the original question remains open, and there is a known candidate graph that may serve as a counterexample.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
status_evidence.snippet: Recently this problem was solved in a weaker setting of extended Cayley algebra, but it is not clear if it is possible to avoid additional elements... There is an example of a graph for which the systems describing codimension 1 strata are not known.
status_evidence.claim: The Cayley-system description of codimension-1 tensegrity strata is a long-standing open problem; only a weaker extended-Cayley version is known.

status_evidence.title: Equilibrium stressability of multidimensional frameworks
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses tensegrity strata and Cayley algebra descriptions in the multidimensional setting.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on tensegrity strata indicates the planar codimension-1 Cayley problem remains open.
